question:
In Data Build Tool (DBT) - a model that is disabled and later referenced returns error.

I have many steps in my project. Sometime I'd rather that certain models will be disabled (no need to rerun them now) - like this:

{{config(
        materialized='incremental',
        enabled=false
    )}}

However, if a model is ref-ed to in another model (like this: {{ ref("MODEL1") }} ) , and I choose to disable that model (just for this specific run) it finishes with an error that I have a dependency to a model that is disabled. I would want it to be able to run it and read from that table as if as it was a source table.

This is a potentially a very complex issue but I am really trying to think of creative solutions.

Eventually my motivation is to be able to run the entire project while dynamically deciding that some models should not be running - and if they are referenced, then I want them to be used as sources and not as a dependency.

Did anyone come across this and managed to find a solution?

I was trying to maybe use some jinja code to deal with each {{ ref("MODEL1") }}, and to determine whether or not that model is enabled - and according to that, set the reference as {{ ref("MODEL1") }} or as {{ source('SCHEMA_NAME', 'MODEL1') }} .

However I'm afraid this path could get very messy..
title: In Data Build Tool (DBT) - a model that is disabled and later referenced returns error
answer:
You can use selectors to decide which models to run on a job execution. In your main project directory (same as dbt_project.yml), create a file called selectors.yml:

selectors:
  - name: my_project_with_tags_ignored
    definition:
      # Run everything except models that are tagged as "dont_run"
      union:
        - method: fqn
          value: "*"
        - exclude:
            - method: tag
              value: dont_run

In your model:

{{
  config({
    "materialized": 'incremental',
    "unique_key": 'some_unique_key',
    "tags": ["dont_run"],
  })
}}
...

To run your job:

dbt run --selector my_project_with_tags_ignored

When you do want to run the model, either do the standard dbt run or create another selector configuration with whatever it is you want included. You can include/exclude whatever combination of tags, model names, paths, etc. Documentation can be found here: https://docs.getdbt.com/reference/node-selection/yaml-selectors
